newsitem.title: USA: Quaker sees 'more rational' cereal promotions.
newsitem.headline: Quaker sees 'more rational' cereal promotions.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co Chairman William Smithburg said he expects the U.S. cereal industry, which reduced prices earlier this year, will take a more rational approach to promotions.
U.S. cereal makers have complained that promotions, such as deep-discount coupons and product give-aways, hurt profitability.
"It is our belief that we and in the industry in general are moving to a more rational promotion approach," Smithburg told a teleconference.
Despite price cuts by major cereal makers this year, category growth remains sluggish.
"On the negative side, the cereal category didn't show growth through the summer," Smithburg said.
He later added that he does not expect the cereal category to slow farther, saying he expects the industry in general to do better.
"This ultimately will be a brand-by-brand game," he said.
For the third quarter, Quaker's ready-to-eat cereals saw a 14 percent volume gain. "Strong consumer francises like Cap'n Crunch and Life cereals are really doing well," he added.
He added that the company's value-priced bagged cereal, which carries the Quaker brand, is growing at more than 20 percent.
Overall, Smithburg said the company's advertising and marketing spending for 1997 should be about the same as in 1996.
"A&M (advertising and marketing) as you look into next year might be flat to up slightly, but clearly Snapple A&M will be down," Smithburg said.

Advertising and marketing spending for Snapple in 1996 was affected by a switch in campaigns this summer. Quaker Oats said the new campaign, which included a nationwide sampling effort, "generated some excitement" but did not produce any financial benefits this year.
In the third quarter, Smithburg said advertising and marketing expenditures for Gatorade and U.S. food -- which are the biggest users of these dollars --- were about flat with a year ago.
Smithburg added that some areas, such as cereal, saw a decline in advertising and marketing expenditures.
